attacks.claim: The revert path is not specified against the postponement and install-window rules. If the 4.7 revert push honours the 14-day postpone or the 02:00-05:00 window, a bad 4.8 can persist on postponing units for up to two weeks, which breaks the agreed 'always able to return' invariant. The revert was also tested on only 300 qa-fleet units.
attacks.evidence: "Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app." / "Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path" / ABSENT: revert timing rules and postponement behaviour for revert pushes

attacks.claim: Rollback deletes every Away Assist user's Home/Away history as an operator action. Users who opted in lose data they did not choose to delete, and no notice or consent step is described for this path.
attacks.evidence: "Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)." / ABSENT: user notice or consent for rollback-triggered deletion

attacks.claim: The downgrade schedule is not deterministic and is not fully surfaced. Periods 5-8 are lost once a 4.7 unit edits, and the 4-period v1 is derived by proximity to anchors with no tie-break, no rule for missing anchors, and no handling of overnight or weekend periods. The only user-facing notice is an in-app message that does not name the removed periods, so a fleet revert can silently change comfort schedules.
attacks.evidence: "keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors" / "The app shows 'Some schedule changes were simplified' if v2 had more than 4 periods." / ABSENT: tie-break rule, missing-anchor rule, 8-to-4 mapping tests

attacks.claim: The interaction between v1-only writers and a stale v2 copy is unspecified. The artifact covers the 4.7-edit case, but not edits made through app 9.2 or other v1-only paths. A later re-upgrade could resurrect an outdated 8-period schedule over a newer edit, and the QA matrix does not test this.
attacks.evidence: "When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy" / "App 9.2 and older can view but not edit 8-period schedules" / ABSENT: rule for v1 writes while a stale v2 exists, and downgrade-then-re-upgrade test without an intervening 4.7 edit

attacks.claim: The Away Assist trigger can set Away while occupants are home. A passive motion sensor cannot see sleeping or stationary people, and a 2 h no-motion rule during a 'home' period may switch to Away setpoints overnight or during quiet activity. The trigger is also underspecified for away-period motion, the 2 h window across period boundaries, and how 'home' maps onto 8 periods. QA has no stationary-occupant case.
attacks.evidence: "sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled "home" periods" / ABSENT: sleep-period exclusion, stationary-occupant test, boundary handling, away-period motion behaviour

attacks.claim: No authentication, authorization, integrity, or replay protection is described for the Home/Away channel from thermostat to cloud or from cloud to app, or for the store. Occupancy-derived data for an account could be read or altered by unauthorized parties. The artifact also does not say whether Home/Away events can influence setpoints, which the impact analysis depends on.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: authn/authz/integrity for the Home/Away channel and store. "Only the resulting Home/Away state is sent to the cloud (needed to show it in the app)"

attacks.claim: Away Assist creates a new category of occupancy-derived data. The claim that it 'does not change existing data sharing' does not address this new collection. Retention in backups, logs, and analytics or telemetry ingest is not stated, so the 7-day deletion claim cannot be verified for the whole system.
attacks.evidence: "Away Assist does not change existing data sharing" / "it is kept 7 days and then deleted" / ABSENT: backup, log, and analytics retention

attacks.claim: The privacy notice goes live with new occupancy-data collection, but the only cited review is a general legal review. There is no evidence of a Canadian (PIPEDA or Quebec) analysis or of the storage region for Home/Away data, despite a Canadian fleet.
attacks.evidence: "Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471)." / ABSENT: Canadian analysis and storage region for Home/Away state

attacks.claim: The public energy claim uses causal wording ('cut heating runtime') and is published on stage-1 day, so a later halt cannot retract it. The control design, sample composition, and variance are not in the artifact, and LGL-4472's approved scope is not stated.
attacks.evidence: "In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%." / "reviewed by legal for substantiation, LGL-4472" / "Release notes (English and French) are published at stage 1"

attacks.claim: There is no Away-specific monitoring. Away activation rate, setpoint changes made by Away, and Away duration are not tracked, so a wrong Away trigger that changes setpoints would not page anyone, and the opt-in cohort may barely exercise the feature at stage 1.
attacks.evidence: "Fleet dashboard by version, rev and HVAC type: boot reverts, self-test failures, offline rate, HVAC fault codes, schedule-sync errors." / ABSENT: Away activation, setpoint-change, or duration metrics

attacks.claim: The stage gates are statistically weak and their enforcement is unclear. At 0.05% on about 6,100 units, the limit is roughly 3 events, so small regressions are not detectable. Paging fires at 0.1%, the advance gate is 0.05%, and no hold or automatic halt is defined for rates between them. Whether stages auto-advance after their stated durations is also unclear.
attacks.evidence: "boot-revert rate < 0.05%, HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline" / "Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% of updated units in any 6 h window" / "Advance only if"

attacks.claim: Install safety during power loss and in power-stealing installs is not tested. The bench list excludes or does not clearly include power-stealing configurations, and no power-cut-during-install test is listed, even though relays are held open for about 90 s.
attacks.evidence: "no C-wire power stealing; rev B/C/D | Pass, 0 relay faults over 72 h" / "During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off)." / ABSENT: power-cut-during-install test

attacks.claim: Automatic revert covers only boot and post-boot self-test failures. HVAC misbehaviour that passes self-test has no automatic revert, so it depends on detection and a manual OTA revert.
attacks.evidence: "If 4.8 fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times, the unit reverts to 4.7 automatically."

attacks.claim: The public timeline is inconsistent with the plan. Stages 1-3 take about 11 days to reach 50%, stage 4 is undated, and postponements can add 14 days.
attacks.evidence: "Rolling out over the next two weeks." / "100% | — | —"

attacks.claim: The anti-rollback counter constraint is not recorded as a release-policy limit. A future security release that increments it would make 4.8 non-installable, so 4.8 cannot be a rollback target.
attacks.evidence: "4.8 does not increment the secure-boot anti-rollback counter (no security fixes in this release), so 4.7 remains installable."

attacks.claim: A revert roughly doubles OTA egress to about 3 TB, and retries are not budgeted. 'Within the monthly commit' is asserted without headroom.
attacks.evidence: "OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB via existing CDN contract, within the monthly commit."

attacks.claim: Home/Away event volume has no rate bound. Motion near the 2 h boundary can flap between states, and the +0.4% ingest projection has no derivation.
attacks.evidence: "Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest."

attacks.claim: The latency from first motion back to schedule is not stated, so a household arriving home may remain on Away setpoints for an unknown period.
attacks.evidence: "returns to schedule on the first motion"

attacks.claim: QA covers the app only. On-device Away and schedule states and French device strings are not tested.
attacks.evidence: "App 9.3 schedule editor and Away Assist screens with VoiceOver, TalkBack, 200% text | Pass"

attacks.claim: Install deferral for temperature has no cap or alert, so a unit could stay on 4.7 indefinitely without anyone noticing.
attacks.evidence: "Install is deferred if indoor temperature is below 7 °C or above 32 °C" / ABSENT: deferral-duration metric or cap

attacks.claim: The v1/v2 dual write, stale-copy discard, and anchor mapping couple firmware, app, and cloud, and no sunset is defined for v1 while 4.7 units exist.
attacks.evidence: "it also writes a v1 schedule (4 periods) on every edit ... the cloud stores both."

attacks.claim: All OTA QA ran on qa-fleet, so campaign behaviour on the public channel at 612k scale (rate limits, CDN caching, cancellation under load) is untested.
attacks.evidence: "delivered through the production OTA service on the qa-fleet channel"

attacks.claim: OTA delivery depends on one existing CDN contract, and no exit path is described.
attacks.evidence: "via existing CDN contract"
